title: Design System: Abdallah Ali Rehab Portfolio

display.purpose: Hero name only — the single largest element on the page.

headline.purpose: Every section title (About, Experience, Skills, Projects, Contact, modal title).

title.purpose: Card titles and sub-block headings (project card names, hero role line).

body.purpose: Paragraph copy — positioning statement, narrative, case-study descriptions.

label.purpose: Eyebrow badges, nav links, chip/tag text, metric captions — often uppercase, wide letter-spacing.

shadows.name: card-hover-glow
shadows.purpose: Standard card/pillar hover treatment, paired with a 4px upward lift.

shadows.name: modal-glow
shadows.purpose: Project case-study dialog ambient halo, present on open (not hover-gated).

shadows.name: app-bar-scroll-shadow
shadows.purpose: Appears only once the app bar compacts on scroll, paired with a real backdrop blur.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default 180-250ms ease-out for hover/press state transitions across buttons, cards, nav links.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Buttons, cards, nav link hover transitions.

motion.name: duration-app-bar
motion.purpose: App bar compact/expand transition on scroll.

motion.name: duration-metric-count
motion.purpose: Hero/impact metric count-up animation (skipped entirely when reduced motion is enabled).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Full-pill accent CTA — used for Download CV, Send Message, and other primary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.1); color: #00F0FF; border: 1.5px solid rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.5); border-radius: 30px; padding: 16px 32px; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.5px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.18s ease-out, border-color 0.18s ease-out, box-shadow 0.18s ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { transform: scale(1.04); border-color: rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.9); box-shadow: 0 0 24px rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.35); outline: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Same shape/padding as Primary but in the neutral text color — lower visual weight (e.g. LinkedIn/GitHub links in the hero).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.05); color: #EAEAEA; border: 1.5px solid rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.2); border-radius: 30px; padding: 16px 32px; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.5px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.18s ease-out, border-color 0.18s ease-out, box-shadow 0.18s ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover, .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { transform: scale(1.04); border-color: rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.35); box-shadow: 0 0 24px rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.15); outline: none; }

components.name: Project Card
components.description: Case-study preview card — icon well, name, tagline, truncated context, up to 3 tech chips, 'View case study' link.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-card-project { background: rgba(26, 26, 46, 0.5); border: 1.5px solid rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.1); border-radius: 20px; padding: 20px; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; transition: transform 0.2s ease-out, border-color 0.2s ease-out, box-shadow 0.2s ease-out; cursor: pointer; } .ds-card-project:hover, .ds-card-project:focus-visible { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.5); box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.15); outline: none; } .ds-card-project-header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 16px; } .ds-icon-well { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 22px; height: 22px; padding: 10px; background: rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.1); border-radius: 12px; color: #00F0FF; } .ds-chip-pill { padding: 5px 10px; background: rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.35); border-radius: 20px; color: #00F0FF; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-card-project-title { color: #EAEAEA; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 700; margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-card-project-tagline { color: #00F0FF; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.4px; margin: 0 0 10px; } .ds-card-project-context { color: rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.7); font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0; }

components.name: Tech Chip
components.description: Small accent-tinted tag for technologies, used inside project cards.
components.css: .ds-chip-tag { display: inline-block; padding: 4px 8px; background: rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.35); border-radius: 8px; color: #00F0FF; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Contact form field — filled, icon-prefixed, floating label, accent focus border.
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: rgba(224, 224, 224, 0.5); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; transition: border-color 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-input-wrap:focus-within { border-color: #00F0FF; } .ds-input-icon { color: #00F0FF; } .ds-input { flex: 1; background: transparent; border: none; outline: none; color: #EAEAEA; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.6); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Desktop top-nav item — animated underline, active/hover accent states.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display: inline-block; margin: 0 4px; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 400; color: rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.7); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; transition: color 0.2s ease-out, border-color 0.2s ease-out, transform 0.2s ease-out; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: #FF007F; border-color: rgba(255, 0, 127, 0.4); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-nav-link--active { color: #00F0FF; border-color: #00F0FF; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Social Icon
components.description: Circular outbound-link icon button (LinkedIn, GitHub) — the one place secondary accent drives the interactive color.
components.css: .ds-social-icon { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 18px; height: 18px; padding: 12px; background: rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.05); border: 1px solid rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.2); border-radius: 999px; color: #EAEAEA; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.16s ease-out, border-color 0.16s ease-out, box-shadow 0.16s ease-out, color 0.16s ease-out; } .ds-social-icon:hover, .ds-social-icon:focus-visible { transform: scale(1.12); border-color: rgba(255, 0, 127, 0.7); color: #FF007F; box-shadow: 0 0 16px rgba(255, 0, 127, 0.25); outline: none; }

components.name: Story Stage Chip
components.description: Signature component — a chain of pill chips connected by forward arrows, tracing a real greenfield/legacy-to-shipped engineering narrative. Only rendered when a project's config supplies real stages.
components.css: .ds-story-strip { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; overflow-x: auto; } .ds-story-chip { padding: 8px 12px; background: rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(0, 240, 255, 0.35); border-radius: 20px; color: #00F0FF; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-story-arrow { color: rgba(234, 234, 234, 0.5); font-size: 14px; }

narrative.overview:
The site reads as a calm, high-stakes systems console at night: near-black surfaces, a slow-drifting starfield, and an orbiting ring of labeled engineering-discipline nodes (Flutter, Architecture, Performance, Security, Testing, CI/CD, Firebase, API) behind the hero. Two accent signals — signal cyan and alert pink — behave like telemetry, not decoration: they mark what's active, what's primary, what just responded to your cursor. Everything else stays disciplined — near-black or near-white surfaces, hairline borders, and generous whitespace — so the accents and the evidence (real user counts, real percentages, real case studies) are what a visitor's eye lands on.

The philosophy is precise and restrained, not loud. Motion exists to confirm interaction (a button scales, a card lifts, a metric counts up once) rather than to perform. The one deliberate rejection the codebase already states outright: no glassmorphism, no heavy gradients. Where the UI feels "glassy" (the pill buttons, the translucent card fills), it's a thin tinted border and a soft fill — never a blurred backdrop panel pretending to be frosted glass. The single exception is the app bar, which does apply a real BackdropFilter blur once scrolled, and it is intentional: a light instrument-panel cue that the console has compacted, not a decorative motif repeated elsewhere.

Depth is ambient, not staged. The system doesn't reserve shadow purely as a hover reward — dark-mode surfaces are already translucent tints over the void (card fills sit at partial opacity over space-black, not flat opaque panels), hairline borders are present at rest, and the starfield/orbit backgrounds give the whole scene a sense of depth before a single element is touched. Hover/focus states then add a directional accent glow on top of that ambient base — an amplification, not the only source of depth.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first "Mission Control" identity: near-black space tones, a starfield, and an orbiting engineering-node motif behind the hero.
Two-signal accent system (signal cyan / alert pink) used sparingly against otherwise neutral surfaces.
Ambient depth at rest (translucent tinted surfaces, visible hairline borders) amplified by accent-tinted glow on hover/focus — never flat-then-nothing.
Outfit throughout, at Material 3's default type scale — no custom font pairing.
Tactile-but-understated components: outlined and tinted, never solid-filled or glassmorphic; every interactive element scales, lifts, or glows in direct response to touch.
A parallel light theme that keeps the same structure and interaction language but trades the starfield/space palette for a plain, high-contrast, WCAG AA-checked surface.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan / Deep Teal appears on active state, primary CTAs, and icon accents only — never as a large fill. If more than roughly one element per view carries full-strength accent color, it has stopped signaling and started decorating.

rules.name: The No-Fabricated-Glass Rule
rules.body: Translucency and thin borders read as "glass-adjacent," but there is no backdrop blur anywhere except the scrolled app bar. Don't add BackdropFilter blur to cards, buttons, or the mobile menu to chase a frosted-glass look — that is the one rejected direction this system already committed against.

rules.name: The One-Display Rule
rules.body: displayMedium (the Display role) is used exactly once per page — the hero name. Every other heading, however large it reads visually, is a Headline or Title. This keeps the name as the unambiguous single largest text element on the site.

rules.name: The No-Shadow-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a boxShadow before it's touched or focused. If a static (non-hover) shadow shows up on a new component, that's a regression against this system's interaction language.

dos: Do treat Signal Cyan / Deep Teal as the primary interactive signal and Alert Pink / Berry Rose as the secondary one — don't swap their roles or use them interchangeably.
Do keep every card and button flat (no boxShadow) at rest, adding glow only on hover/focus.
Do use Outfit at Material 3's default type scale; don't introduce a second font family.
Do reserve full-pill (30px) radius for buttons/badges and 20-24px for cards/panels — keep the radius scale to these five steps.
Do gate the Engineering Story Strip component on real storyStages data — never invent a narrative arc for a project that doesn't have one.
Do keep the starfield/orbit motif dark-theme-only; the light theme reads on a plain surface by design.
donts: Don't add glassmorphism (backdrop-blur panels) or heavy gradients anywhere outside the already-established scrolled app bar. This is a standing, explicit rejection, not an oversight.
Don't apply a static (non-hover) shadow to any component — it breaks the "ambient translucency at rest, glow on touch" depth model.
Don't fabricate metrics, testimonials, or project facts to fill out a component — every number and case study must trace to assets/config.json or the CV.
Don't let the accent colors cover more than roughly one element's worth of a given view — their power comes from rarity.
